posts.location: Renna's stall at the far end of the waygate marketplace crescent — dark-green oilcloth awning, early afternoon spring light, the boar tusks now on her bench and the commission formally recorded.
posts.narration:
Renna is bent over the bench recording the metal preference when Silas speaks. He does not speak to her. He speaks to Pell — or rather, he opens something toward Pell, and the words are only the surface of it.

"May I convey some things to you," he says, "to help you understand how to shape what you will make?"

He uses Order-Sense the way a man holds a door open — not to show the room, but to let the light through it. He finds the design Pell has in him: the morning on the ridge before the boar came, the cold working up through the mud into his knees, the way she stood three steps off his right shoulder without being asked because she had already read the ground and known where to be. He finds the boar — not the danger of it, but the weight of the moment just before it moved, when they were two people who had not yet said anything plainly and the world held them in that suspension. He finds the kill itself: not a proud thing, but a real one, taken cleanly and together, the first hard thing they did as a pair. He finds the walk back after, when the carcass was slung and neither of them spoke because neither of them needed to. He finds the tusks on the bench in front of them right…

posts.location: Frost-hard clearing two hundred yards north-and-west of the made gate — dead birch and alder at the edges, early-spring dawn, flat pale light. The wolverine's flesh has been eased away; the skeletal frame of Logana stands at the base of the downed tree, four-footed and still.
posts.narration:
You look at the wolverine and know what you are about to do before you have decided it. The Attended End is still open — you have not closed it — and through that open door you can see the full architecture of what remains: bone that held eleven years of hard country, joints that never failed her, a skeleton that the Zone made denser and more deliberate than it should be. You read the sequence before you begin. Flesh decays in a direction. Bone wards in another. You can hold both at once if you are careful.

The first step is Deathsense, run wide — and the full design of the ending lays itself out plain. You know exactly where each bone seats, how the joints will hold when the flesh is gone, where the warding must go to make a guardian rather than a ruin. Order-Sense confirms the design as you build it in your mind. The relay node in the hollow pulses faint and steady beneath the tree roots, and you feel the clearing's lattice-work recognize what you are attempting. The second step is Palework, turned gentle — easing the flesh toward its own ending, not tearing, not forcing. It goes cleanly. The bone emerges pale and dense and exactly as the reading promised.

The warding is where it wrinkles. You lay the guardian-purpose into the bones with the care the craft requires, but the relay node beneath the tree takes an interest it was not asked for — a thread of the Zone's lattice seats itself into the ward alongside your own, and the intention you named arrives in the structure alongside something older and less clear. It is not wrong. It is not entirely yours. You hold it, finish the binding, and call it a complication, not a failure.

Shadow Work comes next — you draw dark into the bone-frame, give it the shape of sustained purpose, and then you reach for the radiant binding that will make it move. The four crafts braid into something that should not exist in an ordinary clearing: the bones rise, settle onto four feet, and stand. They are still. They are waiting. Huginn, who has not moved from the flat stone at the edge of the clearing, turns its head away and then back, the way it does when it is reconsidering something.

You speak her name last. Logana. The adaptation carries — the name seats into the ward the way the Weirmark seated into the gate, and the skeletal wolverine turns her head toward the relay node, then back toward you, then toward the line of trees to the south where Pell and Veth are waiting. Not obedient. Aware. The Zone-thread in the warding has made her partly the Zone's creature, and partly yours, and the two intentions sit in her frame without fighting. That is the best you were going to get here, and it is enough. Veth's voice carries across two hundred yards of Zone ground, measured and plain: still moving, keep pace.

*✦ A braid forms — **Deathsense and Palework** become **The Hollowing Sight**.*

posts.location: A lean-to shelter at the edge of The Thinning settlement, early morning, light bent and strange. The open doorway frames the thin place — trees, grass, the waygate clearing. The air tastes of copper and honeysuckle. Spring melt.
posts.narration:
You push yourself up on your elbows and follow Boo's unblinking stare into the space between the trees.

At first there is nothing — just the bent light, the copper taste, the settlement's sounds distant behind you. Then your eyes adjust, and the space resolves into something that was ALWAYS there and your waking mind had simply refused to hold it.

A figure stands in the thin place where the trees open onto the waygate clearing. They are not quite solid. Light passes through them the way light passes through water — bent, but moving. Their shape is human enough to recognize and wrong enough to make your breath catch: too many joints in the arms, a posture that suggests they are standing and falling simultaneously, a face that shifts when you look at it directly — not changing, but revealing, layer by layer, that there was always more to see.

Boo's ears — both of them, though you were certain a moment ago there was only one — rotate toward you. A statement: *This one came through.*

The figure does not move. Does not seem to see you. But the air around them hums with the same tone that woke you this morning, and you understand with sudden clarity that they are *reading* the valley the way you read a page — taking in everything at once, learning the shape of it. The veil is not just thin here. It is open. And something on the other side has noticed that it can step through.
